L118: Cusco International Airport is considered one of the most difficult airports in the world because of the hight altitude, the difficult winds, and of course the big slope of the runway. L119: Cusco International Airport is considered one of the most difficult airports in the world because of the hight altitude, the difficult winds, and of course the big slope of the runway. With an altitude difference of almost 50 (!) meters between both ends of the runway, pilots have only one direction to land and take off, regardless of the winds, which often make both manouvers a real challenge. The lack of an ILS and the sight of a crashed B737 at the side of the runway aren't helping much either.
L120: This airport is only for skilled pilots - are you one of them?
L121: Features:
L122: - Fully accurate rendition of Alejandro Velasco Astete International Airport, Cusco, Peru (SPZO) and surroundings
L123: - Enhanced Cusco city with extra landmarks and buildings
L124: - Custom mesh
L125: - Sloped runway
L126: - Custom built for MSFS with latest MSFS technologies like dynamic lights, parallax windows and ground materials
L127: - Includes static aircraft for even more authenticity
L128: - Optimized for great performance and visual quality
L129: - Includes tool to fix wrong airport name in MSFS

L208: ItalianCharter Team – Gjanosh61 With over a decade of experience in flight simulation development, I specialize in high‑resolution terrain mesh and VFR scenery enhancements. My work has been widely published on AVSIM Library and Flightsim. to, with thousands of downloads and strong community recognition. Focused on accuracy, realism, and technical innovation, I deliver products that bring new life to underrepresented regions, ensuring pilots enjoy immersive and authentic landscapes.
L209: Product Details
L210: This project does not include LOD optimization, as it is not required for this type of content. Instead, I performed a custom adaptation of default water bodies to ensure proper integration with the new terrain mesh.
L211: Data Sources and Tools
L212: - DEM /DTM data is sourced from Sentinel-1 SAR, processed in SNAP13 for maximum terrain accuracy, reprocessed and optimized for MSFS.
L213: - Mesh Technology: Proprietary, developed in-house,
L214: Key Features
L215: - 10-meter (1/3 arc sec) terrain mesh resolution, based on Sentinel-1 data, offering a dramatic improvement over default SRTM1 (30m) coverage.
L216: - Water body adaptation: default lakes, shorelines, and coastal flats have been flattened and reshaped to match the new elevation model.
L217: - Patch for SEGS Airport (San Cristóbal): default buildings obstructing runway 32 have been removed for better realism and usability.
L218: - Optimized for VFR flying: to fully appreciate the terrain detail, it is recommended to fly below 500 feet AGL.[Button:  show more ][Button:  show less ]

L138: The airport ... Alfonso Bonilla Aragón International Airport (IATA: CLO, ICAO: SKCL) formerly known as Palmaseca International Airport is located between Palmira and Cali, the capital of Valle del Cauca Department, Colombia. It is Colombia's fourth-busiest airport in passenger volume, with 5,600,000 people using the airport in 2016, and third largest in area and construction. The airport often serves as the alternate airport for Bogotá - El Dorado Int'l Airport and other Colombian airports.
L139: The airport is one of the very few secondary airports in Latin America that operates 24 hours a day. This is made possible by the year-round stable meteorological conditions, and its distance from both Cali and Palmira, which means it is not subject to any noise restrictions, allowing aircraft to take off and land at any time of day. The airport has non-stop flights to the United States, Spain, Ecuador, Panama and Peru.[Button:  show more ][Button:  show less ]

The package starts at the Combs-Hehl Bridge just east of Cincinnati through Louisville and updated to extend further west to Cairo where the Ohio joins the Mississippi. A photo showing the area covered is included.
L454: The default bridges have been replaced with 33 individually and accurately modeled bridges with night lighting to realistically represent the real world. Many of these are iconic steel bridges with unique designs. 2 are on the National Historic Register.
L455: The most famous bridge in Cincinnati is the John A. Roebling Suspension Bridge opened in 1866 as the longest suspension bridge in the world at that time. Roebling’s most famous bridge is the Brooklyn bridge which then became the longest at that time.
L456: The Dams, Locks and river traffic barges completely missing or submerged in the default are revealed.
L457: Louisville, the largest city in Kentucky, is famous for the Kentucky Derby at Churchill Downs (POI added), Muhammad Ali, Louisville Slugger, and UPS which operates it’s Worldport Air Hub from Louisville International Airport (KSDF).
L458: Louisville has several bridges of architectural significance. The Big Four Pedestrian Bridge (originally a railroad bridge) has a computer controlled lighting system which allows the public to request a 3 color light scheme of their choosing. The bridge is lit every evening. I have done a Red, Blue, Green configuration for this package.
L459: The new Abraham Lincoln Suspension bridge is completely missing in the sim but the traffic flows as though there was a bridge there. The sim is using mapping from the time when the old bridge had been removed but the new bridge had just started construction. I have put the new bridge in the package but the connecting roads are missing. There were major changes to the road’s spaghetti junction which affected the adjacent Kennedy Memorial bridge.
L460: Fixing the road layout for one bridge would ruin the traffic flow for the other. In the package the Abraham Lincoln Bridge is shown accurately but the connecting roads are under construction.

L157: MMMD MERIDA 2024 International Airport – Mexico
L158: Info:
L159: Manuel Crescencio Rejón International Airport or Mérida International Airport (IATA Code: MID - ICAO Code: MMMD - DGAC Code: MID3) is an international airport located in the city of Mérida, Yucatán, Mexico. It is located in the southern part of the city and is one of four airports in Mexico that has a Control Area Center (Centro Mérida), the others being at the Mexico City International Airport, Monterrey International Airport and the International Airport. from Mazatlán.
L160: Centro Mérida controls air traffic over the southeastern part of the country.
L161: The airport handles both domestic and international flights and is open 24 hours a day. It can handle aircraft as large as the Boeing 747 and Boeing 777, although most of the planes that land there are smaller; The most common are the Airbus A320 and Boeing 737. It is the 8th busiest airport in Mexico.
L162: Details:
L163: Hand-modeled the exteriors of all the main buildings of the airport, as well as the interior of the departure hall of the new second-floor terminal. The air base with its hangars was also modeled as much as possible to recreate some of them in 3D. the aircraft that operate there.
L164: Development characteristics:
L165: - Customized jetways.
L166: - Custom earthenware, taxiway and Runways textures.
L167: - PBR textures in 4K high resolution.
L168: - Custom track textures and aprons.
L169: - Added some sculptures to the outside area of the terminal.
L170: - All heliports for civil and tactical operations are incorporated.

These lights, which are operational at 20 airports across the US, turn red in response to traffic, providing direct, immediate alerts without the need for input from controllers.
L315: This modification simulates the FAA Runway Status Light System and includes Runway Entrance Lights and Takeoff Hold Lights. The lights will remain illuminated (indicating unsafe to enter the runway) until cleared for takeoff by the in-game ATC system, at which point the lights will extinguish (indicating safe to enter the runway).

L111: Norfolk Island is an external territory of Australia located in the Pacific Ocean between New Zealand and New Caledonia, 1,412 kilometres directly east of Australia's Evans Head and about 900 kilometres from Lord Howe Island.
L112: Together with the neighbouring Phillip Island and Nepean Island, the three islands collectively form the Territory of Norfolk Island The Norfolk Island International Airport is the gateway to Norfolk Island for visitors and locals alike, it is one the most important pieces of infrastructure on the island. The first runway was constructed on Norfolk Island with the assistance of the United States Air Force and the first aircraft to use it was a Lockheed Hudson bomber on 25 December 1942.
L113: Today the Island receives five commercial operations per week from Auckland, Sydney and Brisbane. The largest aircraft regularly utilising the Airport is presently the Airbus A320. In addition to regular commercial flights the airport is crucial for medical evacuations to Australia.

Located only 13 miles (21km) from the city center, Auckland Airport is a massive hub for international travel with destinations served all over the world.
L167: NZAA is our most detailed product released to date, with a full airside survey done in cooperation with airport officials. In addition to hand-painted close-up details, you'll experience immersive details on approach or departure, featuring densely detailed control tower interiors, hand painted PBR materials and MUCH more! Packed all into one, highly-optimized product designed to run as smooth as possible on your system.

L215: The aircraft are placed so that they are compatible with AI traffic or aircraft ground traffic, nonetheless we recommend having the option “aircraft ground density” to zero.
